question.problem:
Find the values of $k$ such that the vector $b$ lies in $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 4 \\ -12\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ -6\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -3 \\ k\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 4 \\ -12\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ -6\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -3 \\ k\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-8{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=5 \\ 4{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-3 \\ -12{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=k\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-8 & -3 & 5 \\ 4 & 2 & -3 \\ -12 & -6 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & -3 \\ -8 & -3 & 5 \\ -12 & -6 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ -12 & -6 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & k-9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=k-9.$ Therefore, the system has a solution only if

$$
0=k-9\,⇒\,k=9.
$$
